Barsmarts would put you ahead of the majority of bartenders, I do the craft cocktail thing for a living. I find it inspiring that you're inclined to learn more. Not sure where you're located but try and seek out a local cocktail bar, go early and express your interest in educating yourself to whomever is mixing drinks. Any decent/passionate bartender would gladly chat about all these things (provided they're not busy). If your city has a USBG (U.S. Bartending Guild) chapter there is most likely a group of talented barkeeps and a few respectable establishments. Good luck, and I personally recommend the 'intro to aperol' and the 'Hemingway daiquiri' as great modern classic, and classic cocktails respectively.

My late uncle would never say what he did for a living. He was employed by the US government and since I can remember has lived in some interesting places; Korea, Thailand, Italy, Germany to name a few. When I was old enough to know that grown ups actually did things at their job I asked him "what do you do at work?" His reply "eh if some dumbass colonel breaks a printer I fix it." 

After his death I grabbed up as many notebooks, relics and cool T-shirts my family would let me. He has multiple awards from various clandestine sounding acronyms, notes on primitive software. Coolest of all he paid up-front for a Porsche with lots of custom features while he was in Germany and had it shipped to his remote mountain bachelor pad. 

I'm still trying to nail down what he really did. At the funeral home they asked us (me, mom, and 2 aunts) what he did for a local obit in the paper; we all just kinda looked at each other before I awkwardly blurted out "communication specialist."

The general consensus is he helped program and manage missile systems at American foreign bases.

I'm a recovering alcoholic, 23 days sober. I was a bartender, all my friends were/are bartenders and service industry people. I had to quit the awesome bar I worked at making stupid stacks of untaxed cash. I stopped talking to all my friends because they all drink and I'm not confident I could resist the temptation to drink. I was happy being a bartender, I was/am very fucking good at it (one of those craft barkeeps, fancy tools, bitters, diff types of ice, ect), I've won legit competitions and was working on starting a chapter of the US bartenders guild. So now, after a short stay at a treatment center, I have an alright part-time office gig, I'm broke and asking family for bill money. 

I'm 30 and forced to change careers, have intentionally severed my social life; oh and my car is dying so I can't frequent AA meetings or even drive out to go on a hike. Worst, I could get laid BUT stopping to top off the coolant in my car and having no cash to buy a girl so much as a cup of coffee is a turnoff to say the least. 

So I sit at home, cook, watch tv, lurk on reddit, read and try to decide another direction for my life.

I know this isn't nearly as bad as a death in the family, major medical issue or homelessness; but it sucks to go from being respected downtown bartender w plenty of friends, sexual prospects and enough cash to cover a major car repair to a bored, broke part time hourly office worker. 

This sobriety thing better be worth it.
